newsitem.title: UK: UK approves PowerGen plan for gas turbine station.
newsitem.headline: UK approves PowerGen plan for gas turbine station.

text.p: PowerGen Plc has been given consent to build and operate a 500 megawatt gas turbine generating station adjacent to the Cottam power station in Nottinghamshire, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said.
In a statement, it said the centre would initially operate as a development and test centre. The plan was approved by Richard Page, the junior energy minister.

A joint venture between PowerGen and Germany's Siemens AG, the centre will test and develop a new industrial gas turbine with a nominal capacity of 500 MW for the international power generation market. It aims to demonstrate that high thermal efficiencies combined with low emissions of nitrogen oxides are achievable, the statement added.
The centre will operate for two years after which a replacement turbine will be fitted to allow testing over a longer period under normal generating conditions, the DTI said.
